questions.text: Passage: 'Financial literacy is essential for economic empowerment. When individuals understand concepts like budgeting, saving, and investing, they make better financial decisions. Governments worldwide are incorporating financial education into school curricula to equip young people with these skills.' What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Financial education is being added to school curricula

options.label: B
options.text: Financial literacy leads to better economic decisions

options.label: D
options.text: Saving money is the most important skill

questions.solution: Correct answer: Financial literacy leads to better economic decisions.

questions.text: Passage: 'Despite the rapid adoption of digital payments, a significant portion of India's population still relies on cash transactions. The challenge lies in bridging the digital divide — ensuring internet access, smartphone availability, and digital literacy for all.' What challenge does the passage highlight?

options.label: B
options.text: The digital divide in infrastructure and literacy

options.label: C
options.text: People prefer cash over digital payments

questions.solution: Correct answer: The digital divide in infrastructure and literacy.

questions.text: Passage: 'The new tax reform aims to simplify the compliance process, reduce litigation, and create a more transparent system. Tax experts have welcomed the move, though some concerns remain about implementation timelines.' What does 'compliance' mean in this context?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Following rules and regulations.

questions.text: Passage: 'Artificial intelligence is transforming industries from healthcare to finance. However, concerns about job displacement and ethical use of AI persist. Policymakers face the challenge of harnessing AI's potential while mitigating its risks.' Which of the following best describes the author's tone?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Balanced and cautious.

questions.text: Passage: 'The bank's decision to lower interest rates was driven by the need to stimulate economic growth. Lower rates make borrowing cheaper for businesses and individuals, encouraging investment and consumption.' What can be inferred from the passage?

options.label: B
options.text: The bank wants to discourage borrowing

options.label: C
options.text: The bank is trying to boost economic activity

options.label: D
options.text: Interest rates have never been lower

questions.solution: Correct answer: The bank is trying to boost economic activity.

questions.text: Which of the following legal terms best describes a situation where a person is prevented from denying something they previously admitted to in court?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Estoppel.

questions.text: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established which limitation on Parliament's power under Article 368?

options.label: A
options.text: It can amend any part of the Constitution without restriction

options.label: B
options.text: It cannot alter the Basic Structure of the Constitution

options.label: C
options.text: It requires a two-thirds majority for all amendments

options.label: D
options.text: It allows the President to veto constitutional amendments

questions.solution: Correct answer: It cannot alter the Basic Structure of the Constitution.

questions.text: Under which Act was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India established?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Amendment made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 86th Amendment Act (2002).

questions.text: Which of the following bodies is considered a 'Quasi-Judicial' body rather than a full court?
questions.solution: Correct answer: National Green Tribunal (NGT).

questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Canberra.

questions.text: World Population Day is observed on which date?
questions.solution: Correct answer: July 11.

questions.text: Which of the following books was written by Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Gitanjali.

questions.text: Which is the largest national park in India by area?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Hemis National Park.

questions.text: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Geneva.

questions.text: A contracts to sell a specific painting to B for Rs. 50,000. Before delivery, the painting is destroyed by fire. A refuses to deliver. Who bears the loss?

options.label: A
options.text: B bears the loss because he paid the money.

options.label: B
options.text: A bears the loss because the goods were not delivered.

options.label: C
options.text: The contract is void ab initio.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and B share the loss equally.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A bears the loss because the goods were not delivered..

questions.text: X promises to pay Y Rs. 10,000 if Y stops smoking for one year. Is this a valid contract?

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because stopping smoking is lawful consideration.

options.label: C
options.text: No, because it is against public policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only if Y pays X first.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Yes, because stopping smoking is lawful consideration..

questions.text: A minor signs a contract to buy a bicycle. Later, the minor wants to return it claiming the contract was void. What is the legal status?

options.label: A
options.text: The contract is valid and enforceable.

options.label: B
options.text: The contract is voidable at the option of the guardian.

options.label: C
options.text: The contract is void ab initio (from the beginning).

options.label: D
options.text: The court will decide based on the minor's age.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The contract is void ab initio (from the beginning)..

questions.text: In a dispute between two private companies regarding a supply agreement, Company A sues Company B in a civil court. Which law primarily governs this?

options.label: C
options.text: The Sale of Goods Act / Contract Law principles.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Sale of Goods Act / Contract Law principles..

questions.text: A statute passed in 2023 is found to violate a provision of the Constitution of India. What happens to the statute?

options.label: A
options.text: It remains valid until repealed by parliament.

options.label: C
options.text: It applies only to future cases.

options.label: D
options.text: It becomes valid if approved by the Supreme Court.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It becomes void ab initio..

questions.text: A driver accidentally hits a pedestrian while trying to avoid an obstacle. The driver had no intention to harm anyone. Which legal maxim best supports the argument that this is not a criminal offense?

options.label: A
options.text: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione

options.label: B
options.text: Stare Decisis et non quieta movere

questions.solution: Correct answer: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione.

questions.text: A buyer purchases a defective watch from a seller who had no right to sell it. The buyer later discovers the seller was not the owner. What legal principle explains why the transfer of ownership failed?

options.label: A
options.text: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione

options.label: C
options.text: Stare Decisis et non quieta movere

questions.solution: Correct answer: Nemo Dat Quod Non Habet.

questions.text: A previous court has already decided a case between two parties regarding a land dispute. The same parties try to file a new lawsuit with the exact same facts and arguments. What rule prevents the second trial?

options.label: B
options.text: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione

options.label: D
options.text: Stare Decisis et non quieta movere

questions.solution: Correct answer: Res Judicata.

questions.text: A customer buys a product online without inspecting it first. The product turns out to be defective, but the seller did not make any false claims about its quality. Which principle places the burden of inspection on the buyer?

options.label: B
options.text: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione

questions.solution: Correct answer: Caveat Emptor.

questions.text: A lower court refuses to decide a case differently from a higher court in the same jurisdiction. Which maxim describes this practice of following established decisions?

options.label: C
options.text: Stare Decisis et non quieta movere

options.label: D
options.text: Actus Non Facit Reum Sine Intentione

questions.solution: Correct answer: Stare Decisis et non quieta movere.

questions.text: X offers to sell a laptop to Y for $500. Y accepts the offer via email. Before X ships the laptop, X changes his mind and tells Y he will not sell it. What is the legal status of this situation?

options.label: A
options.text: The contract is void ab initio.

options.label: B
options.text: The contract is valid and binding on both parties.

options.label: C
options.text: X is in breach of contract because an agreement was formed.

options.label: D
options.text: Y can sue X for specific performance immediately.

questions.solution: Correct answer: X is in breach of contract because an agreement was formed..

questions.text: In a criminal trial, D is accused of stealing a wallet. D admits he took the wallet but claims he did so because he was starving and needed food for his child. Which defense principle is most relevant to this argument?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Necessity..

questions.text: Husband H and Wife W are married under the Hindu Marriage Act. H wants to divorce W on the grounds of cruelty. W has filed a petition for maintenance. Which statement is legally accurate regarding their status?

options.label: A
options.text: The marriage is automatically void upon filing for divorce.

options.label: B
options.text: W cannot claim maintenance until the divorce decree is passed.

options.label: C
options.text: H's act of cruelty makes the marriage voidable at W's option, but it remains valid until dissolved.

options.label: D
options.text: Both H and W lose all property rights immediately upon filing.

questions.solution: Correct answer: H's act of cruelty makes the marriage voidable at W's option, but it remains valid until dissolved..

questions.text: A law passed by Parliament prohibits all forms of religious procession in public spaces. A citizen challenges this law claiming it violates their Fundamental Right to Freedom of Religion. What is the likely outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The law will be upheld as it is a reasonable restriction.

options.label: B
options.text: The law will be struck down as it violates Article 25/27 (Freedom of Religion).

options.label: C
options.text: The court will refer the matter to Parliament for review.

options.label: D
options.text: The citizen has no right to challenge a Parliamentary law.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The law will be struck down as it violates Article 25/27 (Freedom of Religion)..
